title: Suspension is not enforced on existing sessions, and a banned user can erase their own ban via DELETE /me
claim: authenticate() in server/src/db.ts:129-147 selects only `user_id, last_used` from `sessions` and never looks at `users.banned_at`. The only ban checks are at index.ts:198 (new sign-ins) and links.ts:182 (`createShare`). `live()` at links.ts:139-144 does not consider whether the share owner is banned, and `putPoster` has no ban check. `deleteAccount` at index.ts:383-391 runs `DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?`, which removes `banned_at` along with the row, so the next Discord login creates a fresh account through `upsertDiscordUser`. `closeAll(reason)` at hub.ts:178 is only ever called from `deleteAccount`; there are no admin/moderation HTTP endpoints (moderation is done by hand with `wrangler d1 execute`), so nothing runs `Hub.closeAll` or deletes sessions when someone is suspended. A suspended user keeps a working session, presence, relays, friend requests, live share links/media and poster swaps; only `POST /shares` is refused.
scenario: Repro with seeded user C (`banned_at` set, live session): `GET /me` -> 200; WebSocket hello -> C's presence ('Banned Game') reached friend A; a relay from C was delivered to A. On banned user B: the existing share page and media still return 200 and `PUT /shares/:id/poster` -> 200; only `POST /shares` -> 403. `DELETE /me` by C -> 200 and the users row (including `banned_at`) is gone. Scenario: someone shares abusive clips and the operator sets `banned_at`; their 180-day session keeps working, they keep using presence, sending clips to friends and sending friend requests, their live links stay up and they can swap a link's poster (the `og:image` Discord embeds show) to any JPEG; then they run `DELETE /me`, sign in again with the same Discord account and get a clean account with fresh quota. Capability needed: a suspended user who still holds a token (the normal case, because nothing deletes sessions on suspension).
fix: In db.ts authenticate: `SELECT s.user_id, s.last_used, u.banned_at FROM sessions s JOIN users u ON u.id = s.user_id WHERE s.token_hash = ?`; `if (!s || now - s.last_used > SESSION_IDLE_MS) throw new HttpError(401, ...)`; `if (s.banned_at !== null) throw new HttpError(403, "This account is suspended.")`. In links.ts live(): `... FROM shares s JOIN users u ON u.id = s.owner WHERE s.id = ? AND u.banned_at IS NULL`. Keep bans outside `users` (a `banned_discord_ids` table checked in `authCallback` before the upsert), or refuse `DELETE /me` while banned, or keep a minimal row. Add a cron 'suspension apply' step: find users with `banned_at` set and `suspended_applied_at IS NULL`, delete their sessions, take down their shares (R2 + tombstone), and call `HUB.getByName(id).closeAll("suspended")` (avoids a new admin HTTP surface). Also check the ban in `putPoster`.

The only banned_at reads are index.ts:198 (authCallback, after upsert) and links.ts:81-85/182 (createShare). links.ts:139-143 live() checks only pending/deleted_at/expires_at, used by sharePage:344, shareFile:380, reportShare:330. links.ts:273-288 putPoster: owned() + deleted_at only. hub.ts:241-263 relayFrom checks only areFriends; hub.ts:177 comment says closeAll is for 'gone or suspended' but grep shows its only caller is index.ts:389. index.ts:387 `DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?` drops banned_at; sessions/shares cascade (0001_init.sql:20, 0002_shares.sql:5 ON DELETE CASCADE), so the weekly count also resets. db.ts:96-99 upsertDiscordUser looks up by discord_id; with the row gone it INSERTs a new row with banned_at NULL, so index.ts:198 passes. No moderation tooling or docs exist (server/README.md, server/scripts, tools/ have none); 0005_moderation.sql:1 states intent 'A suspended account can neither sign in nor share'. sessions idle out after 180 days, refreshed daily (db.ts:126-145), so an active user's token never expires.

Filtering live() by the owner's ban, plus a cron step that deletes sessions and shares and calls Hub.closeAll, covers existing links and open sockets. Hub.relayFrom/friendPresence should also skip banned peers, or rely on the closeAll.

title: A 60-second Hub alarm per online user burns the Free-plan Durable Object request quota
claim: The Hub arms a 60-second alarm per online user (hub.ts:33,76,135). Alarm invocations count as Durable Object requests: 1,440 per day for each always-online user.
scenario: Against the Free-plan 100k Durable Object requests per day, that caps the service at roughly 70 always-online users, before counting presence RPCs. Severity: Medium on Free plan.
fix: Sweep every 5 minutes, or skip re-arming when every socket was auto-pinged recently.

votes.evidence: server/src/hub.ts:33 `const SWEEP_MS = 60_000;`. hub.ts:75-77 arms it on connect when no alarm is set: `if ((await this.ctx.storage.getAlarm()) === null) { await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + SWEEP_MS); }`. hub.ts:135 re-arms it on every run while any socket is open: `if (this.open().length > 0) await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(now + SWEEP_MS);`. Nothing skips re-arming when every socket pinged recently. hub.ts:126 only closes sockets idle for over STALE_MS (100 s). One Hub per user (index.ts:85 `env.HUB.getByName(me)`), so it is one alarm per online user, not per socket. The app holds the socket for the whole session and pings every 30 s (src-tauri/src/friends.rs:31-33, 452-488), so a user is 'online' whenever ClippiBoy runs. 86,400/60 = 1,440 alarm runs per day per always-online user, and 100,000/1,440 ≈ 69. The project targets free tiers elsewhere (shares.ts:4 'Everything lives in R2's free tier', shares.ts:13-14 'the free plan').
votes.reachable_by: Ordinary use. Every signed-in app that stays connected keeps its user's Hub waking once a minute. The quota impact assumes the account is on the Workers Free plan.
votes.fix_assessment: A longer sweep interval (for example 5 minutes, and STALE_MS still decides what is stale) cuts alarm requests about 5x for a slower cleanup of half-open sockets. The fix is sound. Skipping the re-arm altogether would leave half-open sockets showing as online forever, so keep at least a slow sweep.

title: POST /t/ping is unauthenticated and unthrottled; each fresh-UUID ping writes ~6 D1 rows kept 400 days, exhausting the shared daily write quota
claim: `POST /t/ping` (telemetry.ts:83-111) has no rate limit; the only check is the body shape. Each ping with a fresh random UUIDv4 inserts into `installs` and `install_days`; counting their PK and secondary indexes, that is roughly 6 D1 'rows written' per request, and the rows are kept 400 days. The D1 database and its Free-plan daily limits (about 100k rows written, 5M rows read) are shared by the whole app.
scenario: A script sends ~20k pings per day (about one every 4 s) and exhausts the free D1 write allowance. After that every D1 write fails until 00:00 UTC: sign-in, `sessions.last_used` touches, uploads and friend actions. On a paid plan, unbounded growth and billing take the place of the outage. No capability is needed. Confirmed in code; the platform limits (Free plan inferred from code comments) are a 'likely' assumption. Severity: High on Free plan, Medium on paid.
fix: Add a rate-limit binding `PING_LIMIT` keyed by `CF-Connecting-IP` (for example 5/60 s), as `REPORT_LIMIT` already does without storing the address. Turn off `workers_dev`, or WAF rules can be bypassed through it. Optionally drop pings whose `version` is not a known release.

ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE ..., INSERT INTO install_days ... ON CONFLICT(id, day) DO UPDATE ...])`, with no limiter. The only rate limit in the Worker is REPORT_LIMIT (wrangler.jsonc ratelimits; links.ts:319, used only by reportShare). migrations/0006_usage.sql:14-34: `installs(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY ...)` + `CREATE INDEX installs_source`, `install_days(... PRIMARY KEY (id, day))` + `CREATE INDEX install_days_day`, so a fresh id writes about 3+3 table/index rows. Rows are swept only after 400 days (telemetry.ts:18, 114-120). Plan context: shares.ts:4 and :14 ('R2's free tier', 'the 100 MB a Worker request on the free plan may carry') point to the Free plan. But ping is not the only open write path. index.ts:136-143 authStart, also unauthenticated and unthrottled, runs `DELETE FROM logins WHERE created_at < ?` and then `INSERT INTO logins ...` on every GET /auth/start that has any 43-char challenge. Upserts with a repeated id also count as writes, so fresh UUIDs matter for storage growth and stats pollution, not for using up the quota. git history: a9013a6 (move to api.clippiboy.com) is an ancestor of e30de21 (pings added), so every build that pings uses api.clippiboy.com (friends.rs:31).
votes.corrected_claim: The code claim holds. POST /t/ping is unauthenticated and has no rate limit. Each accepted ping writes D1 rows: about 6 with indexes for a new id, fewer for a repeated id. A new id's rows stay up to 400 days. On the Free D1 plan, roughly 17k scripted pings a day could use up the daily write allowance. The online features (sign-in, share links, friends) would then fail until 00:00 UTC, and the analytics tables can be filled with fake installs. Severity is overstated, though. Local recording, the core product, is not affected. The outage resets every day and loses no data. Ping is also not the only open write path: GET /auth/start (index.ts:136-143) writes to `logins` on every call with no throttle. And on the Workers Free plan, 100k requests a day to any endpoint already take the API down, so ping only makes a DoS that is already cheap about 6x cheaper. That makes this Medium (a DoS of secondary online features plus statistics pollution), not High.
votes.reachable_by: Any unauthenticated internet client that can POST JSON to api.clippiboy.com/t/ping or the workers.dev host. No account, token or capability is needed, and fresh UUIDv4s are trivial to generate. The same open write path exists through GET /auth/start.
votes.fix_assessment: A per-IP `PING_LIMIT` rate-limit binding is correct and cheap, and it caps D1 writes from one address. On its own it is not enough. Blocked requests still count toward the Workers Free daily request quota, distributed sources get around a per-IP key, and /auth/start stays an open write path, so it needs the same limiter (or a shared `ANON_WRITE_LIMIT`). Turning off workers_dev would break the friends feature for old builds that still use the workers.dev host (wrangler comment). A smaller fix: in the Worker, refuse /t/ping unless the host is api.clippiboy.com, which is safe because every pinging build uses that domain. Then add a zone WAF rate-limit rule on api.clippiboy.com for /t/ping and /auth/start, which stops requests before the Worker runs. Optionally accept only known `version` strings and cap new installs rows per day.

title: GET /auth/start is unthrottled and runs a full-table DELETE on logins (no created_at index), so D1 reads grow quadratically
claim: Each unauthenticated `GET /auth/start` (index.ts:139-143) runs `DELETE FROM logins WHERE created_at < ?`, and `logins` has no index on `created_at`, so every request scans the whole table. It then runs an INSERT that touches the table plus 2 unique indexes. There is no rate limit. R requests inside 10 minutes cost about R^2/2 rows read.
scenario: 3,000 requests inside 10 minutes cost about 4.5M rows read, which is close to the whole Free-plan daily D1 read allowance (5M) shared by the entire app. No capability is needed. Severity: High on Free plan, Medium on paid.
fix: Add an `AUTH_LIMIT` rate-limit binding keyed by `CF-Connecting-IP`. `CREATE INDEX logins_created ON logins(created_at)`, and move the logins cleanup into the cron. Turn off `workers_dev` so WAF rules cannot be bypassed.

votes.evidence: server/src/index.ts:58 `if (path === "/auth/start" && method === "GET") return authStart(url, env);` is routed before `authenticate` (index.ts:72). index.ts:134-143: the only gate is `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/.test(challenge)` (any string works), then `DELETE FROM logins WHERE created_at < ?` and `INSERT INTO logins (state, challenge, created_at)`. migrations/0001_init.sql:28-34: `CREATE TABLE logins (state TEXT PRIMARY KEY, challenge TEXT NOT NULL, code TEXT UNIQUE, user_id TEXT, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL);`. No migration adds an index on created_at (grep for `logins` in migrations/ matches only 0001). wrangler.jsonc:32 has only `REPORT_LIMIT`, which is used only in links.ts:319 (reportShare). The hourly cron (index.ts:46) runs sweep/sweepUsage, and neither touches logins. So each request scans every row created in the last 10 minutes, giving R^2/2 rows read for R requests (3,000 requests is about 4.5M). A sustained rate r per second keeps 600r rows, so reads grow as 600r^2 per second. wrangler.jsonc:12 `"workers_dev": true` leaves a second hostname that zone WAF rules do not cover.
votes.corrected_claim: The code claim and the arithmetic are right. The severity framing overstates the impact. In normal use the table holds a handful of rows, so this matters only under deliberate abuse, and abuse only takes down the online features: sign-in, friends/presence and share links. Local recording is untouched. On the Workers Free plan the same outage class can already be reached without this bug: 100k requests/day is the Worker request cap, and every authenticated route also reads D1. This bug makes the attack about 30x cheaper (around 3k requests instead of around 100k), but it does not open a new capability. On a paid plan it is a cost and overload amplifier: at about 100 requests/s the table holds about 60k rows, and the full scans overload the single D1 database or bill heavily for rows read. Medium, not high.
votes.reachable_by: Any unauthenticated internet client that loops GET https://api.clippiboy.com/auth/start?challenge=<any 43 base64url chars>, or the same path on the workers.dev hostname. No account, cookie or Discord interaction is needed.
votes.fix_assessment: Adding an index on logins(created_at) in a new migration, or moving the DELETE to the hourly cron, removes the quadratic term on its own; either one is the minimal sufficient fix. authCallback (index.ts:173) and authExchange (index.ts:219) already re-check LOGIN_TTL_MS, so rows that expire but linger until the cron are harmless. A per-IP AUTH_LIMIT binding is useful defence in depth against linear flooding, but it is not sufficient alone, because attackers can rotate IPs and the binding is counted per location. Turning off workers_dev would break pre-domain builds that README.md:7 says still use it, so it should wait until those builds are retired, or the workers.dev route should get its own limit instead.

After that it runs `DELETE FROM logins WHERE created_at < ?` (line 139), then `INSERT INTO logins (state, challenge, created_at) ...` (141-143). migrations/0001_init.sql:28-34 `CREATE TABLE logins (state TEXT PRIMARY KEY, challenge TEXT NOT NULL, code TEXT UNIQUE, user_id TEXT, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL);`. title: Two users sending each other friend requests at the same moment get a 500

AND user_b = ?` -> null for both concurrent requests; :331 `if (existing)` skipped; :338-342 plain `INSERT INTO friendships (...) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'pending', ?)` with no ON CONFLICT. Schema server/migrations/0001_init.sql: `PRIMARY KEY (user_a, user_b), CHECK (user_a < user_b)` and pair() orders ids, so A->B and B->A target the same key. The second INSERT throws a D1 UNIQUE constraint error, which is not an HttpError, so index.ts:40-41 returns 500. No transaction or retry wraps the SELECT/INSERT.

title: Presence can arrive at friends out of order
claim: `publish` at hub.ts:219-237 awaits D1 and RPCs, which opens the Durable Object's input gate, so two quick hello/presence messages can interleave. Friends may receive the older presence last and keep showing it.
scenario: A user changes presence twice in quick succession; the two publishes interleave and friends end up displaying the stale first presence. Likely.
fix: Add a sequence number or `at` to `friendPresence` and have receivers drop older ones; or serialize `publish` through a promise chain.

votes.evidence: server/src/hub.ts:219-237 publish(): `const next = this.current(exclude);` ... `await this.ctx.storage.put(PUBLISHED, next);` then `const friends = await friendIds(this.env.DB, user);` (D1, server/src/db.ts:61-69) and `await Promise.all(friends.map(id => this.env.HUB.getByName(id).friendPresence(user, next, lastSeen)...))`. Nothing serializes publish, and webSocketMessage (hub.ts:81-99) awaits it. A DO input gate only holds events during storage operations, so a second message can run during the D1/RPC awaits, compute its own `next` and race to send. A new stub is made per call (`getByName(id)`), so there is no per-stub ordering. The receiver (hub.ts:150-152) broadcasts as it arrives, and the client (src-tauri/src/friends.rs ServerMessage::Presence) does `view.presence.insert(id, presence.clone())` with no sequence or timestamp check.
votes.corrected_claim: The mechanism is right, but a stale result needs the second publish's D1 friendIds query or RPC to overtake the first one's, which is a timing race and not likely. The hello path cannot cause it: hello awaits sendSnapshot before publish, and current() re-reads the attachment, so a later presence message's publish wins and hello's publish then returns early on the equality check (hub.ts:222). Realistic triggers: a quick busy/invisible toggle (src/routes/Friends.tsx:186), a game change, or close-then-reconnect (offline vs online). The sender's stored PUBLISHED is always the newest, so the friend's next snapshot (reconnect or friendsChanged) corrects the stale view.
votes.reachable_by: Any signed-in user whose presence changes twice within a few tens of ms (toggle double-click, a game change landing alongside a config change, a socket close racing a reconnect). Whether the RPCs reorder depends on Cloudflare runtime timing.
votes.fix_assessment: Chaining publish calls through a per-object promise (`this.publishing = this.publishing.then(...)`) removes the interleaving at source. A monotonic sequence number or `at` in friendPresence, with receivers dropping older values, also works and survives cross-stub reordering.

title: Media is publicly cacheable for up to an hour after deletion, and not marked noindex
claim: links.ts:395 sends `public, max-age=min(left, 3600)` on media, so a deleted, moderated or account-deleted clip stays in browser and intermediary caches for up to an hour, although the page promises it is 'removed immediately'. Media responses have no `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, and `api.clippiboy.com/robots.txt` returns 401.
scenario: A user deletes a clip or their account; browsers and intermediary caches keep serving the media for up to an hour. Media can be indexed by search engines.
fix: `private, max-age=300` or `no-cache` with an ETag, and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` on media and on the gone page.

votes.evidence: server/src/links.ts:394-395 `const left = ...; headers.set("Cache-Control", `public, max-age=${Math.min(left, 3600)}`);` on every media response. The X-* headers set at :386-393 include no X-Robots-Tag. Delete paths (links.ts:291-298 deleteShare, :301-306 deleteSharesOf) remove the R2 objects and tombstone the row, and links.ts:380-381 then returns 410, but a cached copy is never revalidated before max-age runs out. site/privacy.html:104 says share links are 'removed immediately' on account deletion. /robots.txt on api.clippiboy.com matches no public route in server/src/index.ts:54-69, so it reaches `authenticate` (db.ts:132 `throw new HttpError(401, "Not signed in.")`) and returns 401. The share page and the gone page already carry `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` (server/src/page.ts:75, through head()).
votes.reachable_by: Any viewer or shared proxy that has fetched the media before deletion keeps a copy for up to 1 h. Cloudflare's own edge does not cache this custom-domain Worker's responses without the Cache API, so 'intermediary' means third-party shared caches or unfurl proxies. Crawlers can reach media only through links posted elsewhere.
votes.fix_assessment: `private, max-age=300` or `no-cache` (the ETag is already set) shortens the window, and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` on media plus a public robots.txt route deal with indexing. Adding noindex to the gone page is redundant, since it already has the meta tag.

title: No 'sign out everywhere'
claim: Session lifecycle gap: there is no way to revoke all of a user's sessions ('sign out everywhere'); only `POST /auth/logout` for the current session exists.
scenario: A user whose token leaked or whose device was lost cannot revoke other sessions.
fix: Add `DELETE /sessions`.

votes.evidence: server/src/index.ts:49-122 route(): the only session-revoking route is `/auth/logout`, at index.ts:87-90, which runs `DELETE FROM sessions WHERE token_hash = ?` for the caller's own token. No route lists or bulk-deletes a user's sessions (grep: the only other sessions statements are the INSERT at index.ts:227 and the SELECT/UPDATE in db.ts:135,144). The app has only friends_sign_out (friends.rs:215-220) and friends_delete_account.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate. The only ways to revoke other sessions are DELETE /me, whose cascade drops all sessions (index.ts:383-387) but also destroys the account, friendships and links, and waiting out the 180-day idle expiry, which a token in active use never reaches.
votes.reachable_by: A user whose token leaked or whose signed-in device was lost or stolen.
votes.fix_assessment: Adding `DELETE /sessions` (all of the user's sessions, optionally keeping the current one) is right. It also has to close the hub sockets (closeAll, or per-session closing as in SV-24), otherwise already-open sockets from the revoked sessions keep working.

title: sweep runs its cleanup steps in sequence, so one R2 error skips the rest including the 30-day report deletion
claim: Within `sweep` (links.ts:419-448) the steps run in sequence without per-step error handling, so an R2 error skips the stale-upload cleanup, the tombstone purge, and the 30-day report deletion (a privacy-page promise).
scenario: A transient R2 failure in the expiry step means stale pending uploads, tombstones and old reports are not purged that hour (or repeatedly, if the failure persists).
fix: Wrap each step on its own.

votes.evidence: server/src/links.ts:426-447: `await env.CLIPS.delete(results.flatMap(...))` (428) and `await env.DB.batch(...)` (429) for expired shares, then stale pending cleanup (435-441), then `DELETE FROM shares WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND created_at < ?` (443-445), then `DELETE FROM reports WHERE created_at < ?` with REPORT_KEEP_MS = 30*DAY_MS (447; shares.ts:141). No try/catch anywhere in sweep; a throw at 428/429 skips everything after. site/privacy.html:101 promises reports are 'deleted after 30 days'.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated. Note the impact of a transient failure is only a one-hour delay (the next hourly run retries everything; the bucket lifecycle rule backs up the R2 objects). The privacy-page promise is only at risk from a persistent failure in an earlier step, and a D1 error (not only R2) in the expiry step has the same effect.
votes.reachable_by: Transient or persistent R2/D1 errors during the hourly cron; not user-triggerable.
votes.fix_assessment: Wrapping each step in its own try/catch with logging is correct; also cheap to move the D1-only retention deletes (tombstone purge, 30-day reports) first so they never depend on R2.

title: Usernames are only synced at login, so two users rows can share a username after a Discord rename
claim: Usernames are only synced at login (db.ts:93-119) and `username` is not unique, so after a Discord rename two rows can share a username.
scenario: User X renames on Discord and user Y takes X's old name; until X logs in again, both rows hold the same username, so a friend request by Discord username can match the wrong account.
fix: Make `username` unique and sync it on use.

votes.evidence: server/migrations/0001_init.sql:7,15 `username TEXT NOT NULL COLLATE NOCASE,` / `CREATE INDEX users_username ON users(username);` (not UNIQUE). server/src/db.ts:100-104 the only sync: `UPDATE users SET username = ?, display_name = ?, avatar = ? WHERE id = ?` inside upsertDiscordUser, whose only caller is the OAuth callback (server/src/index.ts:193-197, after `fetch("https://discord.com/api/users/@me")`); the Discord access_token is used once and not stored. server/src/db.ts:45-46 `SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ?` ... `.first<UserRow>()` returns one arbitrary match. server/src/index.ts:317 `|| (await userByName(env.DB, text.toLowerCase()))` in sendRequest. Sessions last 180 idle days (db.ts:125), so a stale name can persist a long time.
votes.reachable_by: Any two ClippiBoy users where one renamed on Discord and the other later took (and signed in with) the freed name; anyone sending a friend request by that Discord name then may hit the stale row. Impact is bounded: the request is only pending, the response returns the target's display name and avatar (index.ts:335,344 `user: toUser(target)`), and the wrong person must accept.
votes.fix_assessment: A UNIQUE constraint alone would make the new holder's login fail (UPDATE/INSERT conflict) while the stale row keeps the name, and 'sync on use' is not possible because the server keeps no Discord token. Better: in upsertDiscordUser, in one batch, clear the username on any other row that holds the incoming name before writing it (then a unique index becomes safe).

title: Posters can be swapped any number of times
claim: `PUT /shares/:id/poster` (links.ts:273-289) lets the owner replace the poster (the `og:image` in Discord and Twitter embeds) with any JPEG, any number of times, with no limit.
scenario: Costs R2 Class A operations and allows bait-and-switch previews: a link is posted with a harmless preview, then the poster is swapped.
fix: Allow one poster PUT per share, or a few at most.

votes.evidence: server/src/links.ts:273-289 putPoster: `const row = await owned(env, me, id); if (row.deleted_at !== null) throw ...` then size/JPEG-magic checks and `await env.CLIPS.put(poster(id), data, ...)` with no count, no 'already has poster' check and no rate limit; routed for any authenticated owner at server/src/index.ts:75-78. server/src/page.ts:127 `<meta property="og:image" content="${d.poster}">`. The legit app PUTs once (src-tauri/src/links.rs:486-497). It also accepts PUTs on pending and on expired-but-unswept shares, since only deleted_at is checked.
votes.reachable_by: Any signed-in user, on their own shares only (owned() 403s others). The bait-and-switch gain is modest: the first PUT can already be any JPEG (only magic bytes are checked), so the real extra is swapping a reported poster back to something harmless before review; whether Discord/Twitter show a swapped image depends on their embed caching (not checkable here), and shareFile serves the jpg with public max-age up to 3600 s (links.ts:394-395).
votes.fix_assessment: Refusing a second PUT (e.g. a `poster_at` column set with a conditional UPDATE, or R2 `onlyIf` etagDoesNotMatch '*') fits the client, which only PUTs once; also refuse when the share has expired.

title: Privacy page: usage stats called 'anonymous' are actually pseudonymous
claim: The privacy page says usage stats are 'anonymous', with an installation number 'not linked to you'. In practice it is pseudonymous: a persistent installation ID with a per-day profile kept up to 400 days. A unique `/get/<ref>` handed to a single person would identify them.
scenario: An operator hands a unique download ref to one person; their downloads and the resulting installation's daily profile are then attributable to them.
fix: Either commit to never issuing per-person refs, or say 'pseudonymous'.

votes.evidence: server/migrations/0006_usage.sql: `CREATE TABLE installs (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, source TEXT, heard TEXT, first_day, last_day, version)` and `CREATE TABLE install_days (id, day, clips, shots, recordings, features, PRIMARY KEY (id, day))`. server/src/telemetry.ts:100-108 upserts both, keyed by the app's persistent UUID; source is the download ref and is kept with COALESCE (first value wins). telemetry.ts:114-120 sweeps after 400 days. telemetry.ts:9 REF_PATTERN `^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$` accepts any ref name, and site-proxy/index.ts:26-27 counts any /get/<ref>. site/privacy.html:32 says "one anonymous usage count a day", :68 "a random installation number ... which is not linked to you", :75 "Send anonymous usage stats".
votes.reachable_by: The operator, or anyone who hands one person a unique /get/<ref> link. That person's installation row (source = ref) and its per-day activity for up to 400 days can then be tied to them. Even without that, the data is a persistent per-device ID with a daily history, which is pseudonymous rather than anonymous under GDPR Recital 26.
votes.fix_assessment: Changing 'anonymous' to 'pseudonymous' (or 'without your name or account') on privacy.html:32/:68/:75 and in the settings label, and/or committing to campaign-level refs only, both work. The page already gives an Art. 6(1)(f) legal basis, which is consistent with treating this as personal data.

title: Spec: 'no public counting route anyone could call' contradicted by /get/<ref>
claim: The spec says there is 'no public counting route anyone could call'. `/get/<ref>` is itself that route, and its counts can be forged freely. The spec accepts fake pings but not fake downloads.
scenario: Anyone with a browser User-Agent inflates download counts for any ref.
fix: Rate-limit or otherwise protect `/get` counting (see SV-4), or update the spec.

votes.evidence: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-usage-stats-design.md:35-36 'The proxy writes to the friends database through its own D1 binding, so there is no public counting route anyone could call.' (repeated in server/site-proxy/wrangler.jsonc:17-19). Yet site-proxy/index.ts:26-27 routes any GET /get... to download(), and :67-75 'if (request.method === "GET" && !isBot(request.headers.get("User-Agent"))) { ctx.waitUntil(env.DB.prepare("INSERT INTO downloads ... DO UPDATE SET count = count + 1")...' with no rate limit. telemetry.ts:74-75 'return userAgent !== null && /bot|crawler|spider|.../i.test(userAgent);' means a missing User-Agent or 'curl/x' also counts. The write is queued before the body is returned (index.ts:68-83), so a client can abort after the headers. The spec accepts forgery only for pings (spec line 142 'Faked pings cannot be prevented entirely; for statistics that is acceptable.').
votes.corrected_claim: Reach is wider than 'anyone with a browser User-Agent': any GET without bot/crawler/spider/preview-like words in the UA counts, including requests with no UA at all or curl's default one. Each request needs the release.json and GitHub setup fetches to succeed (site-proxy/index.ts:56-66), but the client does not have to download the body. The spec sentence is meant as 'no separate count-only endpoint', which is literally true, but it wrongly suggests download counts cannot be driven from outside.
votes.reachable_by: Any unauthenticated internet client, by repeated GET https://clippiboy.com/get/<ref> with any non-bot User-Agent or none.
votes.fix_assessment: Either state in the spec that download counts are forgeable like pings, or add a per-IP rate limit binding (as REPORT_LIMIT does) to /get counting, as in SV-4. The rate limit also bounds D1 writes and row growth.

votes.fix_assessment: @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers (miniflare is already in node_modules through wrangler) with local D1 lets the callback and exchange be tested with a mocked Discord fetch. Wiring 'npm test' into a CI workflow is a cheap first step.

title: Missing tests: upload quota race and upload edge cases
claim: No test covers the upload quota race (N parallel uploads), abandoned pending uploads, a body shorter or longer than its Content-Length, or that a non-MP4 gives 415 and leaves no R2 object behind.

AND (${LIVE_BYTES}) + ? <= ?`; links.ts:243 `new FixedLengthStream(bytes)` (shorter/longer body vs Content-Length); links.ts:250-253 on failure `env.CLIPS.delete(video(id))`, `DELETE FROM shares`, `if (mp4.refused()) throw new HttpError(415, ...)`; links.ts:435-441 sweep of `pending = 1 AND created_at <= now - PENDING_MS`; links.ts:261-269 finish-or-410. title: Hourly sweepUsage does a full scan of installs because installs.last_day has no index
claim: The hourly cron `sweepUsage` (telemetry.ts:119) runs `DELETE FROM installs WHERE last_day < ?`. `installs.last_day` has no index, so this is a full table scan every hour (rows read = install count x 24 per day). Fake pings via the unthrottled `/t/ping` inflate it further.
scenario: As `installs` grows (including from fake pings), the hourly full scans consume an increasing share of the Free-plan daily D1 rows-read allowance shared by the whole app. Reported under the 'High on Free plan, Medium on paid' D1-quota finding.
fix: `CREATE INDEX installs_last_day ON installs(last_day)`, and run `sweepUsage` once a day.

votes.evidence: server/src/telemetry.ts:113-119 `/** Run by the hourly cron. */ export async function sweepUsage(...) { ... env.DB.prepare("DELETE FROM installs WHERE last_day < ?").bind(cutoff)`; called from server/src/index.ts:44-45 `scheduled(...) { ctx.waitUntil(Promise.all([sweep(env), sweepUsage(env)])) }`; server/wrangler.jsonc:29 `"triggers": { "crons": ["17 * * * *"] }` (hourly). server/migrations/0006_usage.sql:14-22 creates installs with only `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY` and `CREATE INDEX installs_source ON installs(source)`; no other migration indexes last_day (grep INDEX over migrations). Running 0006 in an in-memory SQLite: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN gives `SCAN installs` for the installs delete, while the install_days and downloads deletes use `SEARCH ... USING INDEX install_days_day (day<?)` / `sqlite_autoindex_downloads_1 (day<?)`. server/src/index.ts:68-69 routes `/t/ping` to handlePing before authenticate, and the only ratelimit binding (wrangler.jsonc:32) is REPORT_LIMIT, so pings have no throttle; each new random UUIDv4 id inserts an installs row that is kept for 400 days (telemetry.ts:18 KEEP_DAYS).
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated: an hourly full scan of installs, 24 x install-count rows read per day, and fake pings add rows that each stay for 400 days. 'High' overstates the severity, though. On D1 Free (5M rows read/day), real installs alone would need about 200k rows before this scan used up the read allowance, and on Free each fake ping spends several rows-written (table plus PK autoindex plus index entries) against a 100k/day write allowance, which runs out long before the read side does. The fake-ping effect is real but comes downstream of the unthrottled /t/ping. Note also that the proposed index is not free: D1 bills an extra row written for each index entry touched, and every ping assigns last_day.
votes.reachable_by: Automatically by the hourly Cloudflare cron for any install base, and grown by anyone who POSTs valid-looking pings with fresh UUIDv4 ids to the anonymous, unthrottled /t/ping.
votes.fix_assessment: Running sweepUsage once a day (for example a guard on the controller's cron or scheduledTime hour, or a separate daily cron) cuts the reads 24x and costs no writes, so it should come first. The index on last_day removes the scan, but every ping then writes one more index row, and on Free the write allowance is the scarcer one. Rate-limiting /t/ping deals with the amplification at its source.

votes.evidence: server/migrations/0006_usage.sql:14-22: `CREATE TABLE installs (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, ... last_day TEXT NOT NULL, ...); CREATE INDEX installs_source ON installs(source);` (no index on last_day). server/src/telemetry.ts:119: `env.DB.prepare("DELETE FROM installs WHERE last_day < ?").bind(cutoff)`. server/src/index.ts:44-45: `async scheduled(...) { ctx.waitUntil(Promise.all([sweep(env), sweepUsage(env)])); }`. server/wrangler.jsonc: `"triggers": { "crons": ["17 * * * *"] }` (hourly). server/src/telemetry.ts:64-66: cutoffDay() has day granularity, so 23 of the 24 hourly sweeps each day delete nothing yet still scan the table. server/src/index.ts:70: `if (path === "/t/ping" && method === "POST") return handlePing(request, env);` comes before authentication and has no rate limiter, and every new UUID adds an installs row (telemetry.ts:100). The other two DELETEs are fine: install_days uses install_days_day (0006_usage.sql:34), and downloads is covered by PK(day, ref).
votes.corrected_claim: The code claim is accurate, but the severity is overstated. The scan costs about 24 x (installs seen in the last 400 days) D1 rows read per day. That is about 2.4% of the 5M/day Free-plan read allowance at 5k installs, and only becomes significant at around 100k+ installs. On the paid plan (25B reads/month) it does not matter. Fake pings can inflate the table, but that comes from the separate unthrottled /t/ping issue, and those pings use up the much smaller Free-plan write allowance (100k rows/day) first. This finding is an efficiency issue and an amplifier, not a high-severity defect.
votes.reachable_by: The hourly cron, always. The cost grows with the number of real installs. Anyone on the internet can make it worse by POSTing fake pings with fresh UUIDs to the unauthenticated, unthrottled /t/ping endpoint.
votes.fix_assessment: Both parts are correct, but running the sweep once a day is the better minimal fix: the cutoff only changes once per UTC day, so gating sweepUsage on `new Date(controller.scheduledTime).getUTCHours() === 0` (or a separate daily cron) cuts the reads 24x at no cost. The index makes the sweep cheap, but last_day is in the upsert's SET clause, so D1 bills one extra row written per ping per active install. On the Free plan writes are about 50x scarcer than reads, so after the move to a daily sweep the index only pays off if total installs far exceed daily active ones. Rate-limiting /t/ping (a separate issue) is what actually stops the table from being inflated.

votes.evidence: server/wrangler.jsonc: "triggers": { "crons": ["17 * * * *"] } (hourly). server/src/index.ts:44-45: scheduled(...) { ctx.waitUntil(Promise.all([sweep(env), sweepUsage(env)])); }. server/src/telemetry.ts:119: env.DB.prepare("DELETE FROM installs WHERE last_day < ?").bind(cutoff). server/migrations/0006_usage.sql:14-22: installs(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, ..., last_day TEXT NOT NULL, ...); CREATE INDEX installs_source ON installs(source); -- no index on last_day in any migration (grep of migrations/ finds only installs_source). The other two sweep DELETEs are indexed: downloads PRIMARY KEY (day, ref) (0006:10) and install_days_day ON install_days(day) (0006:34). server/src/index.ts:69: if (path === "/t/ping" && method === "POST") return handlePing(request, env); -- before authenticate(), no rate limiter (only REPORT_LIMIT exists, used in links.ts:319). telemetry.ts:100-103: each ping with a fresh UUID inserts a new installs row; rows live until last_day is 400 days old (KEEP_DAYS, telemetry.ts:18).
votes.corrected_claim: Mechanism is correct: the hourly cron's DELETE FROM installs WHERE last_day < ? is a full scan, ~24*N rows read per day for N installs, about 12x what the pings themselves read (one PK upsert per table per install per day). The 'high' severity is overstated for this item alone. On D1 Free (5M rows read/day) real installs alone only matter at about 100-200k installs, far beyond a v0.8.3 app. On the paid plan (25B reads/month) it does not matter. The real exposure is amplification: any internet user can POST /t/ping with random v4 UUIDs, with no auth and no rate limit. Each fake row then gets scanned 24 times a day for up to 400 days. About 200k fake rows, roughly 10-20 days of pings while staying under the 100k/day write quota, would use up the whole Free read quota every day for over a year. But the same attacker can block D1 at once by using up the write quota, which is the larger umbrella D1-quota finding. So this is a secondary, medium-severity amplifier, not a separate high.
votes.reachable_by: The hourly Cloudflare cron (17 * * * *) runs it on its own, every hour, with no input. The table it scans grows through ordinary app pings: one a day per install from src-tauri/src/telemetry.rs:264. It also grows through any internet user who sends forged anonymous POST /t/ping requests with random UUIDs. Nothing upstream throttles or authenticates the route.
votes.fix_assessment: Running sweepUsage once a day is the real fix. The cutoff only has day granularity, so you could gate it on one UTC hour inside the hourly cron. That alone cuts sweep reads 24x. Adding an index on installs(last_day) by itself can hurt on the Free plan: last_day changes on almost every daily ping, so each ping writes an extra index row (about N more writes/day against a 100k/day quota) to save 24N reads against a 5M/day quota. In quota terms that is roughly a wash or worse. Rate-limiting /t/ping per address is what actually limits the fake-row inflation.

fix: Add integration tests for the sweep steps.

Nothing tests the expired-share delete or tombstone (links.ts:421-431), the stale-pending delete (435-441), the tombstone purge `deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND created_at < now-2*WEEK_MS` (443-445), the report delete `created_at < now - REPORT_KEEP_MS` (447), or what happens when R2 fails partway. title: Missing CSP, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and no-store headers on share and sign-in pages

fix: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'sha256-…'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src https://api.clippiboy.com https://cdn.discordapp.com; media-src https://api.clippiboy.com; font-src https://clippiboy.com; connect-src https://api.clippiboy.com; frame-ancestors 'none'`, plus `Cache-Control: no-store` on the callback page.

votes.evidence: server/src/links.ts:372-374 sharePage returns only `{ "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8", "Cache-Control": "no-store" }` (no CSP / frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options / Referrer-Policy). server/src/index.ts:242-247 page() returns only Content-Type and the clearing Set-Cookie, no Cache-Control, although authCallback (index.ts:203-208) embeds `clippiboy://auth?code=${oneTime}` in both an and an inline `
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated: the headers are missing, and only the callback page lacks no-store (the share page already sends Cache-Control: no-store). In practice, no stated scenario can be exploited. Escaping is correct. A framed sign-in flow fails because of the SameSite=Lax state cookie. A cached one-time code is spent on first use and needs the verifier. Framing the share page would at most expose a rate-limited Report button to clickjacking. Referrer leakage is already limited by the browser's default strict-origin-when-cross-origin and by the per-image no-referrer on the avatar.
votes.reachable_by: Only together with a future escaping regression (CSP), or a third-party site framing clippiboy.com/c/<id> (clickjacking the report button, which REPORT_LIMIT limits to 5 per minute per IP).
votes.fix_assessment: Adding frame-ancestors 'none' and no-store on page() is cheap and correct. The proposed `script-src 'sha256-…'` cannot work as written: both inline scripts change with every response (page.ts:274 interpolates the per-share report URL, index.ts:235 the random one-time code), so it needs a per-response nonce or the values moved into data attributes. img-src would also need https://clippiboy.com for the favicon.

title: Idle sessions are rejected after 180 days but never deleted
claim: Session lifecycle gap: idle sessions are rejected after 180 days but the `sessions` rows are never deleted (no sweep); they are kept until the account is deleted.
scenario: Stale session rows (token hashes linked to user IDs) accumulate indefinitely for inactive users.
fix: Have the cron delete stale sessions.

votes.evidence: server/src/db.ts:139-141 `if (!session || now - session.last_used > SESSION_IDLE_MS) { throw new HttpError(401, ...) }`: it rejects the session and never deletes it. The only DELETEs on sessions are index.ts:89 (logout of the presented token) and the ON DELETE CASCADE from users (migrations/0001_init.sql:18-22; deleteAccount index.ts:383-387). The cron (index.ts:44-46) runs sweep (links.ts:419-448: shares and reports only) and sweepUsage (telemetry.ts:114-121: install_days, downloads, installs only). Nothing removes stale sessions.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate. For context, retention matches what the project publishes: privacy.html:88 says 'Signing out deletes it' and privacy.html:104 says data 'stays stored until you delete your account'. The users row for the same person is also kept indefinitely, so stale session rows add only token hashes and timestamps. Those hashes cannot log anyone in, because authenticate rejects them after 180 idle days. Rows pile up only for sessions abandoned without logout: an uninstall, a lost device, or a local sign-out after a 401 (friends.rs:325-333).
votes.reachable_by: Time passing: any user who stops using a device without signing out.
votes.fix_assessment: A one-line `DELETE FROM sessions WHERE last_used < ?` (now - SESSION_IDLE_MS) in the hourly sweep fixes it; sessions_user is the only index, so this scans the table, which is fine at this size.

title: logins rows (user_id + one-time code) are only cleaned up on the next /auth/start
claim: Session lifecycle gap: `logins` rows, which hold `user_id` and the one-time code, are only cleaned up when someone next calls `/auth/start` (the `DELETE FROM logins WHERE created_at < ?` there); there is no cron cleanup.
scenario: With no further sign-in starts, login rows containing user IDs and one-time codes persist indefinitely, including after account deletion.
fix: Have the cron delete stale logins.

votes.evidence: server/src/index.ts:139 `DELETE FROM logins WHERE created_at < ?` (now - LOGIN_TTL_MS) runs only in authStart. index.ts:218 deletes only the row being exchanged. index.ts:202 writes `code` and `user_id` on a successful callback. The logins table has no FK to users (migrations/0001_init.sql:28-34), so deleteAccount's cascade (index.ts:386-387) does not reach it. Neither sweep (links.ts:419-448) nor sweepUsage (telemetry.ts:114-121) touches logins.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate, but the window is smaller than 'indefinitely' suggests. The DELETE at index.ts:139 is global, not per user, so ANY user's next sign-in start removes every stale row. On a live service that is usually within minutes or hours. Only rows whose callback finished but whose exchange never happened carry user_id and code. Rows abandoned at Discord carry neither. After 10 minutes the code cannot be redeemed (TTL check index.ts:219), and it never works without the verifier.
votes.reachable_by: Any sign-in where Discord's callback succeeds but the clippiboy:// hand-off never reaches the app; the leftover rows then live until any user's next /auth/start.
votes.fix_assessment: Moving (or copying) the `DELETE FROM logins WHERE created_at < ?` into the hourly sweep is trivial and correct. Deleting a user's logins rows in deleteAccount would close the post-deletion gap too.

title: Cron uses Promise.all inside waitUntil, so a sweep rejection can cut sweepUsage short
claim: The scheduled handler at index.ts:45 runs `sweep` and `sweepUsage` with `Promise.all` inside `waitUntil`: if `sweep` rejects, the invocation may end while `sweepUsage` is still running.
scenario: An R2 error makes `sweep` reject; the cron invocation ends early and `sweepUsage` does not finish.
fix: Use `Promise.allSettled`.

votes.evidence: server/src/index.ts:45 `ctx.waitUntil(Promise.all([sweep(env), sweepUsage(env)]));` - both are started eagerly and only the combined Promise.all is registered; Promise.all rejects as soon as either rejects, so nothing else in waitUntil keeps the other promise alive. sweep (links.ts:419-448) awaits a D1 SELECT then R2 delete(s); sweepUsage (telemetry.ts:114-121) is a single D1 batch. No try/catch in either.
votes.corrected_claim: Mechanism is right, but the stated direction is the less likely race: an R2 failure in sweep comes only after a D1 SELECT plus an R2 round trip, by which time sweepUsage's single concurrently-issued D1 batch has usually finished. The more consequential case is the reverse - sweepUsage rejecting early (D1 error) settles the waitUntil promise and can cut the multi-step sweep short. Whether in-flight work is actually cancelled once the waitUntil promise settles is workerd runtime behaviour (documented by Cloudflare; workerd ships only as a binary here, so not checkable from source), and whether an already-dispatched D1 batch still commits server-side is unverifiable. Both jobs are idempotent and rerun hourly, so the effect self-heals.
votes.reachable_by: Any transient D1/R2 error during the hourly cron (17 * * * *); not attacker-triggerable.
votes.fix_assessment: Promise.allSettled (or a separate ctx.waitUntil per job) fixes it, but rejected results should then be logged (and ideally rethrown after both finish) so failures still show up in observability instead of being silently swallowed.

title: Account deletion fails for accounts with more than 500 live links
claim: At links.ts:305 account deletion removes all live shares' R2 objects in one R2 `delete` call. More than 500 live shares means more than 1,000 keys in one call, which throws, so `DELETE /me` returns 500. Only reachable for accounts with `unlimited_links` or `QUICK_LINKS_FOR`.
scenario: An `unlimited_links` account with 501+ live shares calls `DELETE /me` and gets a 500; the account cannot be deleted.
fix: Delete in chunks of 1,000 keys.

votes.evidence: server/src/links.ts:301-305: `SELECT id FROM shares WHERE owner = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL` (no LIMIT) then `if (results.length > 0) await env.CLIPS.delete(results.flatMap((row) => [video(row.id), poster(row.id)]));` - two keys per row in one call. The author's own comment at links.ts:427 ('R2 takes up to a thousand keys at once; two per clip') is why sweep uses LIMIT 400. index.ts:383-391 deleteAccount calls deleteSharesOf before `DELETE FROM users`, so a throw surfaces as the generic 500 (index.ts:39-42) and the account is not deleted. Normal accounts are capped by WEEKLY_LIMIT = 3 (shares.ts:11); unlimited comes only from unlimited_links (migration 0005) or QUICK_LINKS_FOR (links.ts:66-69,86).
votes.corrected_claim: Correct; only nuance: the selected rows also include expired-but-unswept and stale pending rows (deleted_at IS NULL), and the condition is temporary - once uploads stop, rows expire after 5 days and sweep tombstones them (400/hour), after which deletion succeeds. That R2 throws (rather than truncates) on >1000 keys is Cloudflare R2 runtime behaviour; miniflare's local R2 (node_modules/miniflare/dist/src/workers/r2/bucket.worker.js #delete) does not enforce the limit, so it cannot be confirmed from local source.
votes.reachable_by: Only operator-granted accounts (users.unlimited_links = 1 or listed in the QUICK_LINKS_FOR secret) holding more than 500 non-tombstoned shares, calling DELETE /me.
votes.fix_assessment: Chunking the key list into batches of at most 1000 (500 shares) is the right, minimal fix.

title: Expiry rounding overstates the time left
claim: shares.ts:98 computes the expiry text with `Math.round(left / DAY_MS)`, which rounds up partial days.
scenario: With 12 hours left the page says 'in 1 day'; with 4.5 days left it says 'in 5 days'.
fix: Use `Math.floor` for days, and show hours below 2 days.

votes.evidence: server/src/shares.ts:95-105 `const left = expiresAt - now; // Rounded, not cut: a link made a minute ago has five days, not four. const days = Math.round(left / DAY_MS); if (days >= 2) return `in ${days} days`; if (days === 1) return "in 1 day";`. At left = 12 h, Math.round(0.5) = 1 -> 'in 1 day'; at 4.5 days -> 'in 5 days'. Shown on the page and in og:description (page.ts:107,204,206). The rounding is deliberate and tested: server/src/shares.test.ts:64 `assert.equal(expiresIn(now + 5 * day - 60_000, now), "in 5 days");`.
votes.reachable_by: Any viewer of a share page in the last 12-36 h of a link (or at any .5-day mark); cosmetic only, it overstates by at most 12 h.
votes.fix_assessment: Plain Math.floor goes against the documented intent and breaks shares.test.ts:64 ('in 4 days' for a fresh link). Keeping Math.round for days >= 2 but showing hours when left < 36 h, or using Math.floor only below 2 days, fixes the 12 h case and keeps the test.

claim: The site proxy is not type-checked by `npm run check`, because the tsconfig only includes `src`.
scenario: Type errors in site-proxy code ship without being caught by the check script.
fix: Not stated explicitly; implied: include the site proxy in the type check.

title: Privacy page: 'No cookies' while api.clippiboy.com sets cb_login
claim: The privacy page says 'No cookies.', but `api.clippiboy.com` sets the `cb_login` cookie during sign-in. It is strictly necessary, so this is a wording issue.
scenario: A reader of the privacy page is told no cookies are set, but the sign-in flow sets one.
fix: Reword the privacy page to mention the strictly necessary sign-in cookie.

votes.evidence:
site/privacy.html:32 '
  • No ads, no cookies, no tracking across sites. ...
    • ' (a blanket statement in 'In short'; line 49 'The site sets no cookies' is scoped to clippiboy.com and is fine). server/src/index.ts:32 'const STATE_COOKIE = "cb_login";' and :154 '"Set-Cookie": `${STATE_COOKIE}=${state}; Path=/auth; Max-Age=600; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`' on /auth/start, which the app opens in the user's real browser (src-tauri/src/friends.rs:201-202 'app.opener().open_url(format!("{SERVER}/auth/start?challenge={challenge}"), ...)'). title: Missing tests: expiresIn boundaries
claim: No test covers `expiresIn` at 12 h, 36 h and 4.5 days.
scenario: The rounding bug that overstates time left (SV-33) went undetected.
fix: Add unit tests at these boundaries.

votes.evidence: shares.test.ts:61-68 tests expiresIn only at 5 days, 5 days minus 1 minute, 1 day + 5 ms, 3 hours and 1 minute. Nothing tests 12 h, 36 h or 4.5 days. The code rounds on purpose (shares.ts:97-98: `// Rounded, not cut: a link made a minute ago has five days, not four.` / `const days = Math.round(left / DAY_MS);`). As a result, 12 h left gives round(0.5) = 1, so "in 1 day". 36 h gives 2, so "in 2 days". 4.5 days gives "in 5 days". The existing line 64 (5 days minus 1 minute is "in 5 days") already pins the round-up near 5 days.
votes.reachable_by: Developers changing expiresIn; anyone viewing a share page sees the text.
votes.fix_assessment: Adding boundary assertions is cheap and sensible. The author has to decide first whether 12 h should read "in 1 day": the rounding is deliberate, so a test alone would not count it as a bug.

title: Report handling: reports never surfaced, owner can destroy evidence, clips expire unreviewed, reports forgeable cross-site
claim: (1) Reports filed via `POST /c/:id/report` are never surfaced to anyone; the operator has to poll D1. (2) The owner can delete a reported clip (`deleteShare` wipes it from R2 and blanks the title), which destroys the evidence. (3) Clips expire after 5 days whether or not anyone reviewed them. (4) Any website can make its visitors' browsers file reports (no-cors `text/plain` POST); the rate limit (`REPORT_LIMIT`, 5/min) is per IP and per Cloudflare location, and IPv6 rotation gets around it.
scenario: An abusive clip is reported but nobody is notified; the owner deletes it (destroying the evidence) or it expires after 5 days unreviewed. A malicious website silently makes its visitors' browsers file reports, and IPv6 rotation bypasses the per-IP limit. Severity: Low-Medium.
fix: Hide a clip automatically after N distinct-IP reports, notify the operator (webhook or email), and move reported objects to a quarantine prefix instead of deleting them.

votes.evidence: (1) server/src/links.ts:331-337 is the only writer of `reports`: `INSERT INTO reports (id, share_id, reason, note, created_at) SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reports WHERE share_id = ? AND status = 'open') < ?`. The only other access is links.ts:447 `DELETE FROM reports WHERE created_at < ?` (30 days, shares.ts:141). No code sets status 'removed'/'dismissed' (migrations/0005_moderation.sql:16) and nothing notifies anyone. (2) links.ts:291-298 deleteShare, owner-only via owned() (links.ts:153), never looks at reports: `await env.CLIPS.delete([video(id), poster(id)]); await env.DB.prepare(TOMBSTONE)...`. TOMBSTONE (links.ts:159) blanks title, game and tags but keeps `owner`. That row is purged only at links.ts:443-445 (`deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND created_at < now - 2*WEEK_MS`). The reviewer missed a worse path: DELETE /me (index.ts:383-387) runs deleteSharesOf (wipes R2) and then `DELETE FROM users`, and that cascades to the shares rows (migrations/0002_shares.sql:5 `ON DELETE CASCADE`), so the uploader's identity is gone too. (3) sweep, links.ts:421-431, tombstones every `expires_at <= now` share and deletes its R2 objects without checking open reports. LIFETIME_MS is 5 days (shares.ts:19). (4) reportShare (links.ts:315-340) has no Origin or Referer check. `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: PAGE_ORIGIN` only controls who can read the response. The page posts `Content-Type: text/plain` (page.ts:274), which is a CORS-simple request with no preflight, so any site can make the request. The limit is keyed on the full address: links.ts:318-319 `request.headers.get("CF-Connecting-IP")` → `REPORT_LIMIT.limit({ key: address })`, 5/60 s (wrangler.jsonc ratelimits). Each IPv6 address in a /64 therefore gets its own budget. Bounds: an attacker must know the 10-character clip id (shares.ts:80), at most 20 open reports per clip are stored (shares.ts:139, links.ts:334), and a report has no automatic effect.
votes.corrected_claim: Points (1) and (3) are accurate. Reports go into D1 and nothing reads, surfaces or resolves them. Expired clips are swept after 5 days whatever their report status. Point (2) overstates the single-delete path. DELETE /shares/:id destroys the video, poster, title, game and tags, but the shares row keeps `owner`, so the uploader can still be identified for about 14 days after the clip was created. The worse case, which the reviewer missed, is DELETE /me: it wipes the R2 objects and cascades away the shares rows, so neither the content nor the uploader identity survives, while the report row stays for 30 days pointing at nothing. The same orphaning happens to any report reviewed more than 14 days after upload. Point (4) is real but low-impact. Cross-site report POSTs are possible and the limit is per full IP address (rotatable inside an IPv6 /64), but an attacker can just as well send reports directly. Forged reports trigger nothing and are capped at 20 open reports per clip. The real harm is that a flood can fill that cap, after which genuine reports are dropped silently while still answered `{ok:true}`.
votes.reachable_by: (1)(3): any reported clip, by design of the current pipeline. (2): the clip's owner via DELETE /shares/:id, or any account holder via DELETE /me. (4): anyone who knows a clip's id, directly or through other people's browsers on a page they control.
votes.fix_assessment: Operator notification (a webhook or email on the first open report), quarantining reported objects instead of deleting them, and blocking owner and account deletion and sweep from destroying objects with open reports all address real gaps. Auto-hiding after N distinct-IP reports is the risky part: it is exactly what point (4) lets a malicious site trigger, so it would need an Origin check, a /64-keyed limit and a high threshold before it is safe.

title: A null or non-object JSON body gives a 500
claim: `body()` at util.ts:16-22 casts the parsed JSON without validating that it is an object, and callers destructure the result (for example index.ts:212), so a `null` or non-object body throws and returns 500.
scenario: Repro: `/auth/exchange` and `/me` PATCH with body `null` -> 500.
fix: Have `body()` reject anything that is not an object; check `typeof code === "string"`.

votes.evidence: server/src/util.ts:16-21 `return (await request.json()) as T;` only a parse failure becomes HttpError(400); JSON `null` parses fine. server/src/index.ts:212 `const { code, verifier } = await body<...>(request);` (also :94 `const { allowRequests } = ...` and :103 `const { query } = ...`) -> destructuring null throws TypeError, which index.ts:38-41 turns into `json({ error: "Something went wrong on the server." }, 500)`. Primitive bodies do not throw: `const {code, verifier} = 5` yields undefined, so index.ts:213 answers 400 `Missing code or verifier.`; /me PATCH with `5` falls through the `typeof allowRequests === "boolean"` guard and returns 200. Missed case: `{"code":{},"verifier":"x"}` passes `!code` and reaches `.bind(code)` at index.ts:215; workerd's D1 binding throws `D1_TYPE_ERROR: Type 'object' not supported` for a plain object -> 500.
votes.corrected_claim: Only a literal JSON `null` body makes the destructuring throw (500) on /auth/exchange (unauthenticated), /me PATCH and /friends/request (both after authenticate). Other non-object bodies (numbers, strings, booleans, arrays) do not throw and get 400 or 200. Separately, an object-valued `code` on /auth/exchange reaches D1 `.bind()` and also gives 500. The only effect is a wrong status code plus a console.error line; no state changes.
votes.reachable_by: Any unauthenticated client POSTing `null` (or `{"code":{}...}`) to /auth/exchange; any signed-in client for /me PATCH and /friends/request.
votes.fix_assessment: Making body() reject anything that is not a non-null plain object fixes the null case for all three callers. The `typeof code === "string" && typeof verifier === "string"` check is also needed, to close the object-valued-code path to D1.

title: Media Range and conditional request handling is wrong (bad ranges return 206 full body, If-None-Match ignored, HEAD reads body)
claim: Media serving at links.ts:383-406 passes Range through without validation: `bytes=999999-`, `bytes=garbage`, `bytes=10-5` and multi-range requests return 206 with the whole object instead of 416 or 200 (production R2 may throw instead, surfacing as the generic 500). `If-None-Match` is ignored (always 200), and HEAD downloads the object body (an R2 Class B operation).
scenario: Repro (local R2 emulator): `bytes=999999-`, `bytes=garbage`, `bytes=10-5` and multi-range requests all returned 206 with the whole object.
fix: Parse `Range` yourself; return 416 if `start >= size` and 200 when the range is unparseable; pass `onlyIf: request.headers` and return 304; use `CLIPS.head()` for HEAD.

votes.evidence: server/src/links.ts:383 `env.CLIPS.get(key, { range: request.headers })` with no `onlyIf`; :397 `const ranged = request.headers.has("Range") && object.range !== undefined;` :406 `status: ranged ? 206 : 200`. workerd sends the raw header to the R2 backend as `rangeHeader` (string found in the workerd binary). In the local emulator, miniflare r2/bucket.worker.js:520-524 keeps the range only when `parseRanges(...)?.length === 1`, otherwise it falls back to :955-956 `r2Range = defaultR2Range` ({offset:0,length:size}). parseRanges (shared/index.worker.js:582-615) returns undefined for `bytes=garbage`, `bytes=10-5` and `bytes=999999-` (start >= length), and multi-range gives length > 1. So object.range is always set, and the Worker answers 206 with `Content-Range: bytes 0-(size-1)/size` and the full body. :405 does use `CLIPS.get` for HEAD and only drops the body afterwards. If-None-Match is never passed, so the response is never 304.
votes.corrected_claim: The Range mislabelling is real for the local emulator: for a malformed, inverted, unsatisfiable or multi range, the Worker sends 206 with the whole object instead of 200 (ignore the Range) or 416. What production R2 does with such a rangeHeader (ignore it as miniflare does, or throw so the request becomes a 500) cannot be checked from source. Ignoring If-None-Match is allowed by HTTP and only wastes transfer once max-age expires. For HEAD, R2 bills head() as a Class B operation just like get(), so switching saves only the unread body stream, not an operation class.
votes.reachable_by: Anyone with a share link, sending a hand-crafted or unusual Range header. Normal browser video players send valid single ranges (`bytes=0-`, `bytes=N-`) and are unaffected.
votes.fix_assessment: Parsing Range in the Worker (one range; 416 with `Content-Range: bytes */size` when start >= size; ignore it and send 200 when it is malformed or multi), then passing an explicit {offset,length} to R2, fixes the status codes. Adding `onlyIf: request.headers` with a 304 path and `CLIPS.head()` for HEAD are optional optimizations.

title: Logout and suspension do not close an already-open WebSocket
claim: Session lifecycle gap: the bearer token is only checked when the `/ws` socket connects (index.ts:82-91), so logout and suspension do not close a socket that is already open.
scenario: A user logs out (or is suspended) while connected; their existing WebSocket keeps receiving presence and relays.
fix: Call `closeAll` on logout of the last session or on suspension.

votes.evidence: server/src/index.ts:71 authenticate runs once per request; index.ts:82-85 forwards /ws to the Hub with only `X-User`. index.ts:87-90 logout deletes the session row and never contacts the Hub. hub.ts:67-73: the socket attachment stores {user, ready, invisible, presence, at}, with no session or token. hub.ts:119-136: the alarm closes only sockets that stopped pinging (STALE_MS), and pings are auto-answered (hub.ts:56), so a live socket stays open indefinitely while it keeps receiving presence (hub.ts:150-152) and relays (hub.ts:158-163) and can send relays (hub.ts:241-264, which checks only areFriends). Suspension: db.ts:129-147 authenticate never checks banned_at. banned_at is read only at sign-in (index.ts:198-199) and share creation (links.ts:181-182), and no server code ever sets banned_at or calls closeAll on suspension (closeAll's only caller is deleteAccount, index.ts:389). title: The MP4 checker has no cap on box count (CPU exhaustion)
claim: The MP4 box checker at shares.ts:173-216 iterates boxes with no limit on how many top-level boxes a file may contain.
scenario: Bench: a 50 MB file made of 6.5M 8-byte boxes takes about 1.1 s of CPU in V8 (a normal file takes 0.2 ms). It passes the check, and on the Free plan it runs past the CPU limit and stalls the isolate.
fix: Refuse files with more than about 100k top-level boxes.

votes.evidence: server/src/shares.ts:173-216: push() appends header bytes one at a time (`this.header.push(chunk[i++]); this.readHeader();`), and readHeader accepts any box with size >= header length (`size < h.length || size > MAX_BYTES` -> bad), so 8-byte boxes are legal and `this.boxes` is counted but never capped. Reproduced with a copy of the class in node v22 (scratchpad bench/mp4bench.mjs): 50 MB of ftyp + 8-byte boxes = 6,553,598 boxes, accepted (end() true), 1189 ms wall / 1217 ms CPU, ~1.5 ms per 64 KB chunk; a normal ftyp/moov/mdat file takes 0.28 ms. links.ts:250-253: a refused upload deletes its row (`DELETE FROM shares WHERE id = ?`), so a variant without moov fails at flush after the full CPU cost without consuming the weekly quota.
votes.corrected_claim: The CPU amplification is real (~1.2 s CPU per 50 MB vs <1 ms), but the scenario's details are wrong: the work is spread over transform() callbacks of ~1.5 ms per chunk, so it does not stall the isolate continuously; and on the Free plan's 10 ms CPU limit such a request would be terminated (the upload fails) rather than 'pass the check and run past the limit' - it passes only under the Paid plan's 30 s default. The real lever is that rejected uploads (e.g. no moov) leave no row, so one authenticated account can repeat it indefinitely (up to 3 concurrent, bounded by the INSERT's RECENT < WEEKLY_LIMIT on pending rows), each costing the attacker 50 MB of upload bandwidth.
votes.reachable_by: Any signed-in (Discord) account via POST /shares with a crafted body up to 50 MB.
votes.fix_assessment: A cap of ~100k top-level boxes is safe even for fragmented MP4 and removes the amplification; parsing the 8/16-byte header without per-byte array pushes would also cut the constant factor.

title: Friend requests: no rate limit or pending cap, and 404 vs 403 responses enable user enumeration
claim: `POST /friends/request` (index.ts:313-345) has no rate limit and no cap on outgoing pending requests, and Discord usernames can be guessed. The response distinguishes 404 (no such user, or they blocked you) from 403 (allow_requests is off), which reveals which Discord accounts use ClippiBoy.
scenario: A script spams friend requests by guessed Discord usernames and uses the 403/404 distinction to learn which Discord accounts use ClippiBoy.
fix: Rate-limit; cap outgoing pending requests at around 20; return the same answer for 403 and 404.

votes.evidence: server/src/index.ts:102-105 routes POST /friends/request straight to sendRequest with no limiter (the only ratelimit binding is REPORT_LIMIT, wrangler.jsonc:32, used only in links.ts:319). sendRequest (index.ts:313-345): 404 when `!target || isBlocked(target, me)` (318-321); `if (target.allow_requests !== 1) throw new HttpError(403, ...)` (337); otherwise INSERT pending with no count condition (338-342) and `return { status: "sent", user: toUser(target) }` (344). userByName is an exact match on users.username (db.ts:45-47). allow_requests defaults to 1 (migrations/0001_init.sql:12).
votes.corrected_claim: No rate limit and no cap on outgoing pending requests are true. But the 403/404 split is the minor oracle: since allow_requests defaults to 1, the main enumeration channel is the 200 'sent' response, which returns the target's id, username, display name and avatar; an attacker can then withdraw it with DELETE /friends/<id> (index.ts:107-111, removeFriend at index.ts:360-365), leaving the target only a brief flash. Making 403 look like 404 would hide only users who turned requests off, so it does not prevent enumeration; per-account rate limiting is the effective mitigation. Re-requesting after a decline is also unbounded until the target blocks.
votes.reachable_by: Any signed-in (Discord-authenticated) account with a script, guessing Discord usernames or 8-character friend codes.
votes.fix_assessment: Rate-limiting per account (e.g. a Workers ratelimit binding keyed by user id) and capping outgoing pending requests address the spam and slow enumeration; unifying 403/404 is cosmetic on its own because the success path still confirms existence.

title: Site proxy GET /get/<ref> lets any browser-UA client add D1 writes to the shared database, with unbounded new refs kept 400 days
claim: In the site proxy, `/get[/ref]` (site-proxy/index.ts:67-75) adds +1 to `downloads(day, ref)` in the same D1 database whenever the request is a GET from a non-bot User-Agent, with no rate limit. `ref` is any `[a-z0-9-]{1,32}`, so every new ref creates a row kept 400 days. The count happens even if the client aborts right after the headers.
scenario: Any client with a browser User-Agent repeatedly requests `/get/<new-ref>`, adding D1 writes to the database shared with the friends Worker (contributing to the app-wide daily write-quota outage) and creating 400-day rows; download counts can be forged freely. Severity: High on Free plan, Medium on paid.
fix: Add a rate-limit binding or a WAF rule for `/get` in the site proxy; optionally cap distinct refs per day.

The write is started before the Response is built (index.ts:76-83), so aborting after headers does not undo it. The only precondition is that release.json and the GitHub setup fetch succeed (index.ts:56-62). server/src/telemetry.ts:9 `REF_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$/`; :69-71 refFromPath keeps any matching ref (anything else becomes "site"); :74-75 `isBot(userAgent) { return userAgent !== null && /bot|crawler|spider|.../i.test(userAgent); }`, so a missing UA or `curl/8.x` counts as a real download. Retention: telemetry.ts:18 `KEEP_DAYS = 400`; :118 `DELETE FROM downloads WHERE day < ?`, run by the hourly cron (server/wrangler.jsonc:29, src/index.ts:44-45). Same DB: site-proxy/wrangler.jsonc:20-26 binds database_id 67470f4b-... `clippiboy-friends`, the same one as server/wrangler.jsonc. Its comment (site-proxy/wrangler.jsonc:17-19, `Written here directly, so there is no public route anyone could call to count`) misses that /get itself is that public route. No `ratelimits` binding in site-proxy/wrangler.jsonc; the friends Worker has one (server/wrangler.jsonc:32, REPORT_LIMIT) but only for reports.
votes.corrected_claim: The mechanism is accurate. A few details: the file is server/site-proxy/index.ts, not site-proxy/index.ts. No browser UA is needed: any UA that misses the bot regex counts, and so does no UA at all (isBot(null) === false), so a plain curl loop works. A new (day, ref) row also writes the implicit primary-key index (probably about 2 D1 rows written, but that rests on D1 billing and cannot be seen in source). /get is not the only unauthenticated, unthrottled writer to this shared DB: POST /t/ping (server/src/index.ts:68, telemetry.ts:83-110) takes a fresh random UUID per request and writes two upserts (installs and install_days, each with secondary indexes), so it is an equal or stronger quota-burning vector. 'High on Free plan' rests on plan and limits that are not in source. Also, on Workers Free the same request volume (~50-100k/day) against any route already reaches the account's daily Workers request cap, so /get adds only a modest amount on top.
votes.reachable_by: Any unauthenticated internet client sending GET https://clippiboy.com/get/<any [a-z0-9-]{1,32}> with a non-bot or missing User-Agent; it can abort after headers.
votes.fix_assessment: A Workers rate-limit binding (like the existing REPORT_LIMIT) or a WAF rate rule on /get is the right fix, and the abuse goes away if counting is skipped when over the limit. Capping distinct refs, e.g. counting only refs from an allow-list or KV list and mapping unknown ones to 'site', would stop unbounded 400-day rows and forged per-ref stats. /t/ping needs the same treatment, or the shared-DB quota exposure stays.

Each new [a-z0-9-]{1,32} ref per day creates a row kept 400 days, and download counts can be forged freely. Two details are wrong or overstated. votes.evidence: server/site-proxy/index.ts:26-27 `if (/^\/get(\/|$)/.test(url.pathname)) return download(..., refFromPath(url.pathname));` | :67-74 `if (request.method === "GET" && !isBot(request.headers.get("User-Agent"))) { ctx.waitUntil(env.DB.prepare("INSERT INTO downloads (day, ref, count) VALUES (?, ?, 1) ON CONFLICT(day, ref) DO UPDATE SET count = count + 1")...` (registered before the body is streamed, so it runs even if the client aborts after headers). server/src/telemetry.ts:9 `REF_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$/`; :74-75 `isBot` is a UA substring blocklist and `isBot(null)` is false, so a missing UA counts too; :18 `KEEP_DAYS = 400`, :118 sweep `DELETE FROM downloads WHERE day < ?`. server/site-proxy/wrangler.jsonc:20-27 binds the same D1 `clippiboy-friends` (id 67470f4b...) and declares no `ratelimits`; server/wrangler.jsonc:32 has only REPORT_LIMIT. migrations/0006_usage.sql:6-11 `PRIMARY KEY (day, ref)` (rowid table + autoindex, so a new ref costs about 2 rows written and a repeat ref about 1). server/src/shares.ts:13-14 confirms the Free plan.

There is no rate limit, the ref is any [a-z0-9-]{1,32}, and rows are kept 400 days. The file is server/site-proxy/index.ts, not site-proxy/index.ts. Severity is overstated. Each counted request is also a Workers request, and on the Free plan the account has 100k requests a day in total. That means /get gives an attacker at most about 2x leverage over flooding any URL on clippiboy.com or api.clippiboy.com, which already takes the backend down with no D1 involved. It reaches about 100k rows written with roughly 50k new-ref requests, against 100k plain requests. SV-2 (/t/ping, about 6 rows per request) is the cheaper route to the same write-quota outage. To stop junk rows, map refs that are not on an allowlist (or a small set of known campaign prefixes) to "other", so the table grows by at most known refs times days. The Hub Durable Object storage (presence, status text, game, last seen) is not pinned to a jurisdiction (no `jurisdiction("eu")`), so it is created wherever the user first connects.

Every caller uses the plain namespace: server/src/index.ts:85 `env.HUB.getByName(me)`, index.ts:299 `env.HUB.getByName(id).friendsChanged()`, index.ts:389, hub.ts:233 `this.env.HUB.getByName(id).friendPresence(...)`, hub.ts:257, hub.ts:270 `.card()`. grep finds no `jurisdiction` or `locationHint` anywhere in server/src.
