fix: Add tests for these cases.

votes.evidence: The only server tests are src/shares.test.ts, src/telemetry.test.ts and scripts/e2e.mjs (git ls-files). None of them call handlePing (telemetry.ts:83), reportShare (links.ts:315) or body() (util.ts:16). util.ts cannot even be loaded by `node --test` (see telemetry.ts:5-6: "util.ts uses syntax type stripping does not cover"). e2e.mjs only posts a valid object `{code:"x",verifier:"y"}` to /auth/exchange and never hits /t/ping or /c/<id>/report. Not covered: chunked or oversized bodies on any of the three. Already covered: null JSON for the ping and report validators. telemetry.test.ts:37 passes `null` and expects cleanPing to return null, and shares.test.ts:129 has `assert.equal(cleanReport(null), null)`. Both validators start with `if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object") return null`, so an array also gives 400 (telemetry.ts:37, shares.ts:145).
votes.corrected_claim: Untested: oversized or chunked bodies on handlePing, reportShare and body(), and null or array bodies on body() callers (index.ts:94, 103, 212), which is where the SV-15 500 comes from. Null and array JSON on the ping and report routes cannot 500: cleanPing and cleanReport reject them, and both are unit-tested with null.
votes.reachable_by: Developers changing the request-handling code; the gaps hide unauthenticated DoS-style body reads (/auth/exchange, /t/ping, /c/<id>/report) and the body() null 500.
votes.fix_assessment: Worth adding handler-level tests, but body() lives in util.ts, which plain `node --test` cannot load. That needs Miniflare or vitest-pool-workers, or moving the size guard into an import-free module like telemetry.ts. Note that no CI workflow runs `npm test` in server/ at all.

title: Missing tests: Range and conditional requests
claim: No test covers Range and conditional requests: unsatisfiable, multi-range, suffix ranges, `If-None-Match`, HEAD.
scenario: The incorrect 206-with-full-body behaviour (SV-18) went undetected.
fix: Add tests for these cases.

votes.evidence: shareFile (links.ts:378-407) is never exercised by any test or by e2e.mjs. Only the pure helper byteRange is tested, and that test includes a suffix range: shares.test.ts:73 `assert.deepEqual(byteRange({ suffix: 50 }, 1000), { offset: 950, length: 50 })`. There are no tests for unsatisfiable or multi-range requests, If-None-Match, or HEAD. Two notes from the source: (1) If-None-Match is not implemented at all. links.ts:383 passes only `{ range: request.headers }` and no `onlyIf`, so a test would be checking behaviour that does not exist. (2) In miniflare, an invalid or multi-range header makes `validate.range` return undefined (bucket.worker.js:521-524). R2 then reports the full default range (bucket.worker.js:955-956), so `ranged` is true at links.ts:397 and the response is a 206 with the whole body. Only an R2-backed integration test, not a byteRange unit test, would expose that.
votes.corrected_claim: Suffix ranges are covered at the byteRange level (shares.test.ts:73). What is missing is any handler-level test of shareFile: unsatisfiable, malformed and multi-range requests, HEAD, and conditional requests (which are not implemented).
votes.reachable_by: Developers changing media serving; anyone who sends crafted Range headers to /c/<id>.mp4.
votes.fix_assessment: Handler tests against Miniflare R2 would catch the 206-with-full-body bug. If-None-Match support has to be built (by passing onlyIf or checking the ETag) before it can be tested.

title: Missing tests: site proxy
claim: No test covers the site proxy: `refFromPath`, HEAD not counted, bots not counted, the Location rewrite, and pinning of `release.setup.url`.
scenario: Regressions in download counting, the Location rewrite (SV-37) or release URL pinning (SV-14) go undetected.
fix: Add tests for these cases.

votes.evidence: Nothing tests the site-proxy worker (site-proxy/index.ts) itself: the Location rewrite (lines 37-42), the GET-only and non-bot counting gate (line 67, `request.method === "GET" && !isBot(...)`), and HEAD returning a null body (line 83) are all untested. Two of the listed items are tested, though. refFromPath has its own test at telemetry.test.ts:47-54 (`/get/tiktok1`, upper case, `/get`, `/get/`, `/get/Bad!`, a 33-character ref). isBot is tested at telemetry.test.ts:56-68, covering Discordbot, Googlebot, facebookexternalhit, WhatsApp, TelegramBot, Embedly and null. And release.setup.url is never pinned: line 61 is `file = await fetch(release.setup.url, { method: request.method })` with no origin check. A test of pinning would test a feature that does not exist.
votes.corrected_claim: refFromPath and the bot detection (isBot) are unit-tested in telemetry.test.ts. What is untested is the site-proxy handler: the Location rewrite (including the `//` case from SV-37), the rule that only GETs from non-bots are counted, and HEAD handling. release.setup.url has no pinning to test; SV-14 needs that code first.
votes.reachable_by: Developers changing site-proxy/index.ts; download-count accuracy and the redirect behaviour on clippiboy.com.
votes.fix_assessment: Handler tests with a stubbed fetch and D1 would cover the rewrite and the counting gate. For SV-14, the URL check must be written first, and then tested.

title: Note: MP4/HTML polyglots are accepted; safety relies on fixed video/mp4 type plus nosniff
claim: The MP4 checker accepts an MP4/HTML polyglot (ftyp + moov + size-0 mdat + HTML). This is by design, and it is safe only because media is served with a fixed `video/mp4` type plus `nosniff`.
scenario: Repro: the polyglot was accepted. If the fixed Content-Type or `nosniff` were ever dropped, the upload could be interpreted as HTML.
fix: Keep the fixed `video/mp4` type and `nosniff` (and document the polyglot case in tests).

votes.evidence: server/src/shares.ts:176 `if (this.toEnd) return true;` and :208-209 `if (size === 0) { this.toEnd = true; }` mean any box of size 0 swallows the rest of the upload. :191 `end()` accepts `(this.skip === 0 || this.toEnd) && this.moov`. The doc comment at :158-160 already says so: "What it cannot rule out is a payload inside a box ... served as video with `nosniff`, which is what keeps such a file a (broken) video." Reproduced by running a copy of shares.ts under node 22 in the scratchpad: ftyp+moov+size-0 mdat+HTML -> true; ftyp+moov+`free` box holding HTML -> true; ftyp+size-0 moov+HTML -> true. Serving: links.ts:247 `env.CLIPS.put(video(id), ..., { httpMetadata: { contentType: "video/mp4" } })` is set by the server and never comes from the client; links.ts:387 `object.writeHttpMetadata(headers)`, :391 `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, :392 `Content-Disposition: inline`. Media is served from MEDIA_ORIGIN `https://api.clippiboy.com` (links.ts:34). shares.ts:203 requires the first box to be `ftyp` with size 16..1024, so byte 0 of every accepted file is a binary size byte (0x00), not '<' or whitespace.
votes.corrected_claim: Polyglots really are accepted, and through more than a size-0 mdat: a `free`/`skip`/`mdat` box of normal size with HTML in it, or a size-0 moov, also passes. The doc comment at shares.ts:156 ("anything hung on behind, fails") does not hold for a size-0 last box. The comment at :158-160 already admits the polyglot case, so it is known. The safety reasoning is overstated, though. What matters is the declared `video/mp4` type, which the server sets itself (links.ts:247). Browsers do not turn a response declared as video/mp4 into HTML whether or not nosniff is sent, so losing nosniff alone changes nothing. Because the checker forces a binary ftyp header at offset 0, the HTML-sniffing patterns (which match only at the start, after whitespace) would not match even with no Content-Type at all. The file would sniff as MP4 or octet-stream. The case that would actually make it HTML is a regression that labels the object text/html (or similar), and no client input can cause that.
votes.reachable_by: Any signed-in, non-banned account can upload such a file through POST /shares (createShare, links.ts:171) within its weekly quota. It only becomes dangerous if a future server change serves R2 objects with an HTML-capable Content-Type. No client-controlled path does this today.
votes.fix_assessment: Keeping the server-fixed video/mp4 type and nosniff is right, and so is adding a test that pins the polyglot case. Also fix the shares.ts:156 comment. Defense in depth could serve media from a cookieless origin separate from the API (api.clippiboy.com carries the cb_login state cookie and the API) or add `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`. Only re-encoding would actually rule out embedded payloads.

title: workers_dev: true lets anyone bypass zone-level WAF and rate-limit rules
claim: The friends Worker has `workers_dev: true`, so it is reachable at its `*.workers.dev` address in addition to `api.clippiboy.com`, which lets anyone bypass zone-level WAF and rate-limit rules.
scenario: An attacker targets the workers.dev address to avoid any WAF or zone rate-limit rule added for api.clippiboy.com.
fix: Turn off `workers_dev`.

votes.evidence: server/wrangler.jsonc:9-12 `// The app talks to api.clippiboy.com. The workers.dev address stays on, so builds from before the domain keep working.` ... `"workers_dev": true,`. README.md:7-8,22-23 keeps the workers.dev URL as a registered Discord redirect, and scripts/e2e.mjs:11 defaults to it. The only rate limits in source are hostname-independent and run inside the Worker: wrangler.jsonc:32 REPORT_LIMIT binding used at links.ts:318-319, and the relay limits in the Hub DO. No zone WAF or rate-limit rule is defined or referenced anywhere in the repo.
votes.corrected_claim: The Worker really is reachable at clippiboy-friends.fabian081964.workers.dev, on purpose, for pre-domain builds. That only bypasses zone-level WAF or rate-limit rules if such rules exist on the clippiboy.com zone, and none are defined here. Every limit the code itself enforces (the REPORT_LIMIT binding, the Hub relay caps) applies on both hostnames. So this is a defence-in-depth note, not a present bypass. That workers.dev traffic skips zone rules is Cloudflare platform behaviour and cannot be checked from source.
votes.reachable_by: Anyone, but only against zone-level rules that the owner adds in the Cloudflare dashboard; nothing in the repository is bypassed today.
votes.fix_assessment: Turning workers_dev off breaks builds from before the domain (and the e2e default and the second Discord redirect), so it needs those builds to be retired first. Until then, keep any protective limits inside the Worker (rate-limit bindings), where they cover both hostnames.

title: QUICK_LINKS_FOR is read from env through a cast and missing from secrets.d.ts
claim: `QUICK_LINKS_FOR` reaches `env` through a cast (links.ts:67) and is missing from `secrets.d.ts`.
scenario: Type checking cannot catch a misspelled or missing `QUICK_LINKS_FOR` binding.
fix: Not stated explicitly; implied: declare `QUICK_LINKS_FOR` in `secrets.d.ts` and drop the cast.

votes.evidence: server/src/links.ts:66-68 `const list = (env as Env & { QUICK_LINKS_FOR?: string }).QUICK_LINKS_FOR ?? "";`. server/src/secrets.d.ts:2-4 declares only `DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET: string;`, and the generated worker-configuration.d.ts:4-10 __BaseEnv_Env has no QUICK_LINKS_FOR. It is the only use site (grep). tsconfig.json includes src, so a declaration in secrets.d.ts would be picked up.
votes.corrected_claim: The cast exists and secrets.d.ts omits the variable, but the stated consequence is overstated. QUICK_LINKS_FOR is optional by design: unset means 'changes nothing' (links.ts:61-63). TypeScript cannot detect a missing or misspelled secret set with `wrangler secret put`, whether or not it is declared. A code-side misspelling at this single use site would be just as uncaught with a misspelled declaration. Moving the type into secrets.d.ts is a consistency cleanup, not a fix for a reachable failure.
votes.reachable_by: Developers editing the code; no runtime or user-facing effect.
votes.fix_assessment: Declare it as optional (`QUICK_LINKS_FOR?: string;`) in secrets.d.ts and drop the cast. Declaring it as required `string` would be wrong, because it is normally unset.

title: Privacy page: 'Delete account removes everything immediately' is not fully true
claim: The privacy page says deleting the account removes everything 'immediately'. Media can survive in caches for up to an hour (`public, max-age`); `logins` rows stay until the next sign-in start; reports referencing the share IDs stay 30 days (they hold no personal data).
scenario: After account deletion, clips remain fetchable from caches for up to an hour and login rows remain until someone next starts a sign-in.
fix: Shorten/privatise media caching and sweep logins in the cron (see SV-19, SV-22), or adjust the wording.

votes.evidence: site/privacy.html:104 lists only 'your account, sign-ins, friendships, blocks, online status and share links are removed immediately'; it does not say 'everything'. deleteAccount (server/src/index.ts:383-391) does remove each of these in the request: R2 objects via deleteSharesOf (links.ts:301-306), 'DELETE FROM users' with ON DELETE CASCADE on sessions/friendships/blocks/shares (migrations/0001_init.sql:20,38-39,49-50; 0002_shares.sql owner REFERENCES users ON DELETE CASCADE), and Hub storage via closeAll -> 'await this.ctx.storage.deleteAll()' (hub.ts:177-187). Residue that is real: links.ts:395 'headers.set("Cache-Control", `public, max-age=${Math.min(left, 3600)}`)'; logins.user_id has no FK (0001_init.sql:28-34) and stale rows are only removed by 'DELETE FROM logins WHERE created_at < ?' in authStart (index.ts:139); a consumed login is already deleted in authExchange (index.ts:218). Reports keep only share_id/reason/note (0005_moderation.sql) and are swept after 30 days (links.ts:447).
votes.corrected_claim: Every item the page lists is deleted server-side, synchronously, in DELETE /me. A new request for a deleted clip gets 410, because the share row is cascade-deleted and live() returns null (links.ts:139-143, 381). The cache residue is only in the HTTP cache of a viewer who already loaded the clip or poster; it can replay from there for up to an hour. Cloudflare does not put responses a Worker generates into its edge cache unless the Cache API is used, which this code does not do, so a new viewer cannot fetch the clip from any cache we run. That part rests on platform behaviour and cannot be checked from source. The logins leftover only exists for a login that went through the callback but was never exchanged. It holds an orphaned UUID, an unused code and a challenge hash, and the next /auth/start by anyone removes it. The page does not list logins among the deleted items ('sign-ins' means sessions, privacy.html:88). This is a minor wording or retention nit, not a false promise.
votes.reachable_by: Any user who deletes their account. The only exposure is a viewer who had already opened their share link and replays it from that viewer's own browser cache within the hour.
votes.fix_assessment: Switching media to 'private, max-age=...' (or no-cache with ETag) and adding a logins sweep to the hourly cron (SV-19, SV-22) would remove the remaining edge cases cheaply. Adjusting the wording alone would also be acceptable.

title: README: sessions 'expire after 180 days' but rows are kept
claim: The README says sessions 'expire after 180 days'. They are rejected after that, but the rows are kept until the account is deleted.
scenario: Session rows of long-inactive users persist indefinitely despite the documented expiry.
fix: Delete stale sessions in the cron (see SV-21).

votes.evidence: server/README.md:36-37 'Sessions are stored as hashes and expire after 180 days without use.' server/src/db.ts:125 'const SESSION_IDLE_MS = 180 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;' and :139-141 'if (!session || now - session.last_used > SESSION_IDLE_MS) { throw new HttpError(401, ...) }', before the touch at :143-145, so an expired session never revives. No code deletes expired rows: sweep() (links.ts:419-448) and sweepUsage() (telemetry.ts:114-121) never touch sessions. Rows are only removed by logout (index.ts:87-90 'DELETE FROM sessions WHERE token_hash = ?') or by the cascade on account deletion (0001_init.sql:20).
votes.corrected_claim: The facts are right: idle sessions older than 180 days are rejected but their rows (token_hash, user_id, created_at, last_used) stay until logout or account deletion. The README is not actually contradicted, though. It says the sessions 'expire after 180 days without use' and they do, because the code refuses them. It never promises deletion. The privacy page also says this data 'stays stored until you delete your account' (privacy.html:104), so what is stored is disclosed. The real issue is a storage-limitation gap that keeps dead rows, the same as SV-21, not a documentation error.
votes.reachable_by: Passive: any user who stops using a device without signing out leaves an unusable session row behind indefinitely.
votes.fix_assessment: Adding 'DELETE FROM sessions WHERE last_used < ?' (now - SESSION_IDLE_MS) to the hourly cron is a one-line fix and makes the wording literally true. It belongs with SV-21.

title: Missing tests: Mp4Boxes edge cases
claim: No test covers `Mp4Boxes` edge cases: size-0 box to the end of the file, 64-bit largesize, size smaller than the header, `ftyp` over 1 KB, very many tiny boxes (CPU), and the documented polyglot case.
scenario: The box-count CPU issue (SV-28) and regressions in box parsing go undetected.
fix: Add unit tests for these cases.

votes.evidence: shares.test.ts:85-109 has three Mp4Boxes tests, all built with a `box()` helper that always writes size = 8 + body: whole MP4 in 1- and 1000-byte chunks; `an ftyp glued in front of something else fails` (ftyp size 8 + ZIP `0x50,0x4b,3,4`, and real ftyp + ZIP); `an MP4 with something hung on behind, or without moov, fails` (trailing `0x50,0x4b`, no moov, MZ header). Nothing exercises shares.ts:198/200 (size32 === 1 largesize), shares.ts:208-209 (size 0 -> toEnd), shares.ts:210 `size < h.length` for a non-first box, shares.ts:203 `size > 1024` for ftyp, or a high box count. A probe against the real class (scratchpad sv5x/probe.mjs) shows these branches currently behave correctly: size-0 moov -> true, largesize mdat -> true, size-4 box -> false, 1100-byte ftyp -> false.
votes.corrected_claim: Five of the six cases are untested (size-0 box, 64-bit largesize, non-first box smaller than its header, ftyp over 1 KB, very many tiny boxes). The polyglot cases the doc comment says are caught (shares.ts:155-156: ftyp glued in front, anything hung on behind) ARE tested at shares.test.ts:99-109 with ZIP signatures; only the documented-as-uncatchable payload inside a box has no test. The untested branches work today, so the gap is regression protection; the SV-28 box-count issue is a missing limit that no test would catch until a cap is chosen.
votes.reachable_by: Not a runtime defect; future edits to Mp4Boxes.readHeader.
votes.fix_assessment: Easy to add to shares.test.ts with the existing walk() helper (shares.ts imports nothing, so it runs under the current `node --test`); a box-count test makes sense together with the SV-28 cap.

title: Site proxy Location rewrite can produce a protocol-relative URL
claim: The site proxy's Location rewrite `location.slice("/clippiboy".length)` (site-proxy/index.ts:41) would turn `/clippiboy//x` into the protocol-relative `//x`.
scenario: An upstream redirect to `/clippiboy//x` is rewritten to `//x`, which the browser resolves as a different host. Speculative.
fix: Only rewrite results that start with a single `/`.

votes.evidence: server/site-proxy/index.ts:37-41: `const location = response.headers.get("Location"); if (location?.startsWith(ORIGIN)) {...} else if (location?.startsWith("/clippiboy")) { response.headers.set("Location", location.slice("/clippiboy".length) || "/"); }`. A Location of `/clippiboy//x` does become `//x`, and `/clippiboyfoo` becomes the relative `foo`. The upstream fetch at :29 uses `${ORIGIN}${url.pathname}` with redirect: "manual", so the request path reaches GitHub Pages as sent. The only directories in the published site are site/img and site/fonts (find site -type d).
votes.corrected_claim: The string handling is as described. Whether it ever matters depends on GitHub Pages sending a root-relative Location starting with `/clippiboy//`. That would need (a) GitHub Pages to use relative rather than absolute (https://einfabo.github.io/clippiboy/...) Location headers, which the first branch at :38 already handles, and (b) it to keep a double slash from a request like clippiboy.com//img. Even then the target "host" could only be an existing directory name (img, fonts), because WHATWG URL parsing collapses `..` segments, so an attacker cannot choose a host. The result would be a broken redirect, not an open redirect.
votes.reachable_by: Only a visitor who opens a crafted URL such as clippiboy.com//img, and only if GitHub Pages sends a root-relative Location that keeps the double slash. That cannot be determined from source.
votes.fix_assessment: Cheap hardening: rewrite only when the location is exactly `/clippiboy` or starts with `/clippiboy/`, and collapse a leading run of slashes in the result to one (or always emit an absolute HOME + path). That closes both the `//x` and the `/clippiboyfoo` cases.

title: The download endpoint trusts release.setup.url without pinning it
claim: site-proxy/index.ts:61 streams whatever URL `release.json` (read from Pages) names in `release.setup.url`, served as `ClippiBoy_<v>_x64-setup.<ref>.exe` from clippiboy.com, without validating the URL origin or the version format.
scenario: Any compromise of the Pages content, the bake workflow, or the `einfabo` GitHub namespace makes the official domain serve an arbitrary binary. Severity: Low-Medium.
fix: Require `setup.url` to start with `https://github.com/EinFabo/clippiboy/releases/download/` and `version` to match `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`.

title: Privacy page: share links say 'display name and avatar' but also expose the Discord user ID
claim: The privacy page says share links show 'display name and avatar'. The avatar URL also exposes the Discord user ID (same issue as SV-10).
scenario: Anyone with a share link reads the uploader's Discord snowflake ID from the avatar URL.
fix: Proxy or replace the avatar, or disclose it (see SV-10).

title: Hub Durable Object: unlimited sockets per user, no rate limit on hello/presence, relay budget is per connection
claim: `acceptWebSocket` at hub.ts:66 has no cap on sockets per user. The relay budget (intended 30 per 10 s) lives in `this.relayed`, keyed per WebSocket (hub.ts:248-252), so more sockets multiply it. Every `hello` or `presence` message (hub.ts:89-98) runs `sendSnapshot`, then `publish`: a Durable Object storage write, a D1 `friendIds` query, and one RPC to each friend's Hub, which in turn sends to every one of that friend's sockets; there is no rate limit on these messages. Every relay does a D1 `areFriends` lookup (hub.ts:256), even when the result is 'not a friend'.
scenario: Repro: 4 sockets of one user delivered 119 relays in about 2 s (intended limit 30 per 10 s); 200 presence flips produced 200 fan-out messages at a friend. One free Discord account opens N sockets and spams relays to random UUIDs, or flips its presence; every message costs a D1 read and Durable Object requests or storage writes, draining the account-wide D1 and Durable Object daily quotas for everyone and flooding friends' apps.
fix: Cap sockets per user (e.g. close the oldest beyond 5). Apply one per-connection budget to all message types and close the socket with code 4008 on abuse. Keep the per-user relay budget in `ctx.storage` or in memory per user, not per socket. Cache the friend set in the Hub, invalidated by `friendsChanged`, so relays do not hit D1. Coalesce `publish` calls (debounce about 1 s).

title: 'Appear offline' can be detected through a relay probe
claim: `relay()` at hub.ts:158-162 delivers to every `ready` socket and returns true without checking `attachment.invisible`, so the sender only gets `relayFailed: "offline"` when the target has truly no sockets. An invisible user is therefore distinguishable from an offline one, contradicting the privacy page promise: "With 'Appear offline', friends see you as offline."
scenario: Repro: B said hello with `invisible: true`; A relayed `{id: "probe"}`: there was no `relayFailed`, and B received the probe. Any accepted friend can poll a body that the target's app ignores and learn exactly when an invisible friend is online.
fix: If `this.current() === null` (invisible or offline), do not deliver and answer "offline". Alternatively, have the app opt in per relay. Either way the answer must look the same.

title: Unbounded request bodies are read into memory, including on unauthenticated routes
claim: `body()` at util.ts:16-22 calls `request.json()` with no size limit; it is used by `/auth/exchange` (unauthenticated), `/me` PATCH and `/friends/request`. At telemetry.ts:85-87 the size check relies on Content-Length, which is absent in chunked uploads, then calls `request.text()`. links.ts:324 does `JSON.parse((await request.text()).slice(0, 2048))`, reading everything and then slicing. `putPoster` already guards against this (see its comment at links.ts:276), but these routes do not.
scenario: Repro: a 5 MB chunked body to `/t/ping` was read completely before the 400 came back. Bodies of up to 100 MB (the edge limit) are buffered and decoded, which can exceed the isolate's 128 MB memory and kill other requests running on the same isolate. The report notes severity is Medium-Low in practice because the attacker pays the bandwidth.
fix: A shared `readLimited(request, max)` that streams with `getReader()`, cancels and returns 413 once `max` is passed, and rejects when Content-Length exceeds `max`. Validate that the parsed JSON is an object (this also fixes the null-body 500).

title: A few throwaway accounts can keep the global share bucket 'full' with abandoned pending uploads
claim: shares.ts:18 sets `TOTAL_BYTES = 9 GB` with `WEEKLY_LIMIT = 3` per account. At links.ts:57 a pending upload holds its declared `bytes` for up to 30 minutes, and an aborted upload is deleted (links.ts:252), so it does not use up a weekly slot. Reservations can be re-opened repeatedly at no quota cost.
scenario: About 60 Discord accounts each keep 3 x 50 MB uploads open with a stalled body. Every 30 minutes the reservations lapse and the attacker simply re-opens them. Everyone else gets 507 'Sharing is full' indefinitely, and almost nothing is stored. Real 50 MB uploads from the same accounts do it for 5 days at a time. Likely.
fix: Count a pending reservation against the week even after it is abandoned (keep the row with `aborted = 1` instead of deleting it). Cap how many bytes a single account can have live. Alert on a full bucket. Consider a per-IP rate limit on `POST /shares`.
